answer.why_different: The generated document introduces a different structure: it places reusable schema definitions under `paths./{className}={id}.put.callbacks.components`, apparently confusing the document-level Components Object with the contents of a Callback Object. This also leaves callback-related `$ref` targets unresolved within the document.
answer.spec_3gpp: The specification identifies Resource, Scope, MoiChange, NotifyMoiAttributeValueChanges, and NotifyMoiChanges as data types, but the supplied passages do not support declaring them under an operation callback’s `components` key.
answer.openapi: A callback value must be a Callback Object whose entries are runtime-expression keys mapping to Path Item Objects. The generated `components` block instead contains schema definitions and is therefore not a valid callback structure; the supplied validation also identifies a missing `$ref` and unresolved local references.
answer.clearer_why: The generated block is structurally misleading and invalid OpenAPI 3.0, whereas the official side does not expose this malformed callback definition.

citations.quote: {expression} | [Path Item Object](#path-item-object) | A Path Item Object used to define a callback request and expected responses.
callbacks | Map[`string`, [Callback Object](#callback-object) \| [Reference Object](#reference-object)] | A map of possible out-of band callbacks related to the parent operation.

differences.reason: This is an extra and invalid structural block: the generated side adds `callbacks.components` containing schemas, although callback entries must describe callback operations through runtime-expression keys and Path Item Objects (O1, O4). The block also contains unresolved local references, so it is not merely an equivalent relocation (C2).

#### Callback Object  
A map of possible out-of band callbacks related to the parent operation.
Each value in the map is a [Path Item Object](#path-item-object) that describes a set of requests that may be initiated by the API provider and the expected responses.
The key value used to identify the callback object is an expression, evaluated at runtime, that identifies a URL to use for the callback operation.

Field Pattern | Type | Description
---|:---:|---

```  
Note that in the use of `operationRef`, the _escaped forward-slash_ is necessary when
using JSON references.  
##### Runtime Expressions  
Runtime expressions allow defining values based on information that will only be available within the HTTP message in an actual API call.
This mechanism is used by [Link Objects](#link-object) and [Callback Objects](#callback-object).  
The runtime expression is defined by the following [ABNF](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5234) syntax  
```
expression = ( "$url" | "$method" | "$statusCode" | "$request." source | "$response." source )
source = ( header-reference | query-reference | path-reference | body-reference )
header-reference = "header." token
query-reference = "query." name
path-reference = "path." name

#### Link Object  
The `Link object` represents a possible design-time link for a response.
The presence of a link does not guarantee the caller's ability to successfully invoke it, rather it provides a known relationship and traversal mechanism between responses and other operations.  
Unlike _dynamic_ links (i.e. links provided **in** the response payload), the OAS linking mechanism does not require link information in the runtime response.
